articleTitle: Supercapacitor control for electric vehicle powered by hybrid energy storage system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Pure electric vehicle and hybrid electric vehicles have gained attention in recent years due to concerns about the carbon footprint of internal combustion engines. In recent years, the focus in the electric vehicle research space has been to establish systems that will ensure the maximum life span of the battery. Therefore, research has coupled the battery with a supercapacitor to become a battery-supercapacitor hybrid energy storage system (HESS). The supercapacitor can absorb the high frequency power surges of the EV while the battery supplies the average power of the EV. In this paper, a novel rule-based energy management system (EMS) is proposed. The proposed EMS uses the physical parameters of the EV to limit the battery power rate and amplitude. The simulation results show that the control objectives of the controller were reached with the use of the urban dynamometer driving schedule (UDDS).

articleTitle: Copper vs. aluminium winding SRMs: a multidisciplinary performance assessment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The winding represents an essential element in every electrical machine. Winding design and operating conditions have a direct influence - among others - on torque performance, thermal behaviour, voltage stress distribution and ensuing machine reliability and lifetime. With reference to switched reluctance machines, the winding represents the sole `source of excitation', implying that any modification (e.g., in terms of layout, materials or operating conditions) can strongly affect the capability of delivering shaft torque in a satisfactory manner. Accordingly, this paper aims at investigating, through a multidisciplinary approach, how shifting from copper to aluminium winding can affect the performance of switched reluctance machines. By relying on a purposely designed use-case machine, it is found that in some contexts (or applications) the use of aluminium could provide a higher peak power density, although with a lower thermal margin. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that in an aluminium-winding switched reluctance machine, stator modes of vibration are excited at slightly higher frequencies, potentially leading to a reduction in emitted acoustic noise.

articleTitle: Understanding the limits of a hall sensor sensitivity for integration on a GaN power transistor chip: experiments with market available components
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN) is an emerging wide bandgap technology in power electronics. It enables higher power density, wider operating temperature range and higher efficiency compared to other widely used technologies, allowing miniaturization and overall weight and cost reductions at system level. In contrast, the technology produces high levels of radio emissions and it is prone to failure without an adequate active power monitoring due to its sensitivity to unmatched electrical parameters. Since intrusive monitoring can disrupt the transistor's efficiency on power delivery, galvanic isolated sensors are intensely explored with the goal of chip-level integration on the difficult-to-manufacture GaN structures. The experimental results in this study reveal that in a power monitoring scenario envisaged for the integration on a GaN transistor chip, a Hall sensor that requires a minimum magnetic field threshold of 1 mT will be sufficient. The noisy GaN transistor environment is tested for three different low power loads, resistive, semi-conductive, and inductive, at 1, 5 and 10 kHz, demonstrating that the radiated emissions relate to the load current rather than voltage, whereas the Hall device measurements show stability and consistency.

articleTitle: Soft magnetic composite material integrated FBG flux sensing for electrical machine in-situ flux monitoring applications
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility of achieving flux density sensing capability in electric machinery by integration of soft magnetic composite material (SMC) with electromagnetic interference immune (EMI) fibre optic fibre Bragg grating (FBG) sensors. The sensor's design, fabrication, and performance characterisation are presented, and experiments are performed to evaluate the functional features and the ability of the proposed sensor architecture to monitor the rotating field dynamics typical of electrical machine applications.

articleTitle: Down-scaling of drive cycles for experimental drive cycle analyses
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Modern electric machines operate within a wide range of torque-speed operating points. Real drive cycles of a real vehicle cannot be tested in the given lab with machines that have smaller ranges and thus the drive cycles need to be down-scaled. To allow for experimental investigations of such driving scenarios even in small laboratory scale analyses, this paper presents a method of down-scaling the drive cycles of different vehicles. Three test case speed-over-time drive cycles are chosen and analysed with two different electric vehicles to derive the corresponding torque-speed profiles for the study. These drive cycles are down-scaled to fit the ratings of the two laboratory test case motors. The down-scaling method aims to replicate the torquespeed characteristics of the original driving cycle while considering the specific characteristics of the motors being used in the laboratory. The effectiveness of the proposed down-scaling method is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Analytical modelling for surface-inset permanent-magnet machines accounting demagnetization effects
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This papers proposes a modelling technique for the demagnetization effect in surface-inset permanent-magnet synchronous machines. The geometry of the machine is divided into subdomains and in each subdomain Laplace's and Poisson's equation is solved. By expressing the magnetization functions into a difference of Heaviside functions, the demagnetization effect is accounted by the consideration of the trailing edge of a magnet having a lower value of remanent magnetic flux density. Later on, the function is being inserted on Poisson's equations and the solution is extracted in analytical form. To validate the proposed modelling technique a Two-Dimensional Finite-Element Analysis model was used. Apart from the magnetic flux density distribution the Back-EMF, cogging-torque and the unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP) were also calculated. The proposed analytical model can be used as a tool to offer quick and accurate performance calculations for the impact of demagnetization effects on surface-inset permanent-magnet machines.

articleTitle: Grid-forming control for the linear-generator-based wave energy converter for the electrification of remote islands
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The development of wave energy technology has advanced significantly, and its grid connection and power optimization stages have been an area of research. Various grid connection schemes have been thoroughly researched and are being implemented, while grid-following control has emerged as the primary technique for power transfer to the grid. Energy storage solutions such as batteries and supercapacitors have been incorporated to mitigate the intermittency effect of wave energy. However, with the increase of renewable energy in the grid leading to a low-inertia power grid, wave energy must be equipped with grid-ready capabilities to achieve commercial success. This study proposes a wave-to-wire model for a wave energy converter array in a grid-forming application, enabling the supply of power to remote islands. The results of this research propose the control mechanisms required for the successful integration of wave energy to form a grid and transmit a continuous power supply.

articleTitle: Impact of stator segmentation on forces and vibrations in PM generators for offshore wind power
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The ModHVDC concept is a modular permanent magnet generator which uses insulated stator segments with dedicated power electronic converters to produce HVDC. This could significantly reduce the number of required power conversion steps for HVDC-connected offshore wind parks. However, the concept poses structural challenges to the machine design, which are investigated in this paper. It is observed that segmentation of the stator has two major effects on the harmonic forces that occur inside in the machine: the addition of low spatial order harmonics, referred to as the segment harmonics, and an increase of the cogging torque. Furthermore, the structural integrity of the stator was found to be reduced. Based on these findings, design recommendations are put forward to mitigate the drawbacks of stator segmentation.

articleTitle: Sensorless control of an induction machine with an SOGI based MRAS observer and a phase locked loop
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a sensorless speed control for an induction machine is proposed. The adaptive model reference system (MRAS) based on a second order generalised integrator (SOGI) uses the phase currents and control voltages in combination with the motor parameters to estimate the internal voltages of the machine, from which the rotor speed and position can be calculated. The use of the extended MRAS observer in combination with a phase-locked loop (PLL) should lead to improved dynamics, stability, precision, and a wider speed range of the drive system. First, a field-oriented control (FOC) is implemented in a simulation with the model of an induction machine, in which the function of the MRAS observer can subsequently be tested. In the following, a test bench is set up to implement the control algorithms on a microcontroller. Furthermore, an algorithm for speed estimation via the slip of an induction machine is implemented. The results and measurements listed are exclusively hardware-based and were carry out on the test bench. Finally, the observer is operated in combination with slip compensation in order to compensate for the load-dependent deviation of the mechanical angular velocity of an induction machine.

articleTitle: Performance analysis and optimization of a H-type flux switching linear generator for wave energy converters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Two H-type flux switching permanent magnet linear generators (FSPMLGs) with outer-translator and inner-translator configurations are discussed for use in wave energy converters and compared to a more conventional flux switching topology. The translators consist of six H-Type modules, each of which is surrounded by two permanent magnets (PMs). In conventional FSPM machines the windings are twisted around the PMs, whereas in the H-type topologies the PMs are sandwiched between adjacent coils. The proposed topologies are designed for a low operating speed which is equal to the nominal speed of a wave energy converter. Using finite element analysis (FEA), the H-type topologies and the conventional structure are simulated, and the results are extracted in terms of the magnetic flux density distribution, flux line, thrust force, back emf, and efficiency. All topologies are optimised using the Taguchi optimisation approach with the goals of reducing force ripple and increasing the average thrust force and efficiency. The results of the proposed topologies, and the conventional structure are compared in several aspects such as average thrust force, force ripple, loss, and efficiency.

articleTitle: An enhanced linear active disturbance rejection speed controller for PMSMs
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: For high-performance permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive systems, smooth speed regulation is crucial. The existence of various disturbances will lead to different degrees of fluctuation in the speed. Linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) is recognized as an effective method to suppress disturbance. However, the conventional LADRC speed controller has a steady-state tracking error under ramp load disturbance and cannot suppress periodic load torque disturbances. In this paper, an enhanced LADRC speed controller is proposed. By optimizing the extended state observer and modifying the speed feedback channel, the designed controller can completely eliminate the steady-state tracking error caused by the ramp load disturbance, and effectively suppress the periodic disturbances caused by load torque. This paper theoretically analyzes the anti-interference performance of the proposed method and proves its stability. Finally, it is verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: A hybrid method to determine the average permanent magnet temperature in an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid method to study the permanent magnet temperature in an interior permanent magnet machine (IPMSM) is introduced. The flux-observer based method is applicable for operating points at medium and high speeds and is highly sensitive to the accuracy of the involved machine parameters. The temperature estimation using thermal models requires knowledge of the machine assembly and the heat transfer parameters, for which optimizations and validations of the model are necessary. Consequently, the flux observer and the thermal model are used together to allow a continuous estimation of the temperature development also at zero and low speeds. Cross validations with measurements on a test bench show a high precision of the magnet temperature estimation with a maximum error of 6K for the studied load profile. This work presents a practical approach with low assembly effort to acquire the thermal state of the rotor in IPMSMs.

articleTitle: Sensorless vector control of contra-rotating permanent magnet synchronous motors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the sensorless control of Contra-Rotating Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (CR-PMSMs) is established with a model-based approach. This concept is then validated with a Simulink model, and verified by an experimental set-up with a low-cost Digital Signal Processor/Digital Signal Controller (DSP/DSC) and a customized PMSM. Contra-rotating rotors entail many interesting qualities, compared to a single-propeller arrangement, such as superior efficiency, (gyroscopic) stability and power output for the same propeller radius. Furthermore, sensorless (i.e. without mechanical sensors like encoders) control, with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) as a robust estimator to counteract noise and model uncertainties, renders it a viable candidate for airborne and underwater applications by lowering cost and increasing reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Wave energy power take-off design of hybrid energy storage system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Despite widespread marine wave energy resources, wave energy has not become a mainstream renewable energy source. One reason is the fluctuating power with low average to peak ratio extraction from the wave energy converter. This paper evaluates a hybrid energy storage system in the power take-off, combining a lithium-ion battery and super-capacitor unit, to provide power smoothing. The integration of energy storage into the DC-link through bidirectional DC-DC converters enables effective use of the super-capacitor for extreme short-term power fluctuations, with the battery for long-term power balance. The feasibility of this design to provide DC voltage regulation and absorb fluctuating currents under different states of charge and input sea states is verified through MATLAB/ Simulink with representative power data from a kW-scale 20m wave platform. The half-bridge converter with double-closed-loop PI control is tested in a full-witching simulation model. The obtained results confirm that the designed energy storage can smooth the wave power and balance the benefits of energy density and power density in the battery unit and super-capacitor unit respectively.

articleTitle: Direct sensing of IGBT junction temperature using silicone GEL bonded FBG sensors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In order to safeguard the chips and bond wires, conventional wire-bond IGBT power modules commonly employ a flexible silicone gel filling. This study evaluates the utilisation of the same silicone gel to secure an optical sensor that is installed on the surface of the IGBT chip for the purpose of direct junction temperature measurement. The silicone gel's impact on the in-situ FBG sensor's wavelength-to-temperature (λ-T) characteristics was evaluated throughout its curing process and found to be negligible. Additionally, the thermal sensing performance of the gel bonded FBG sensor was analysed in the nominal operating current range of the test commercial IGBT module and verified against measurements taken with a thermal camera. The findings suggest that the silicon gel provides a suitable bond viscosity for securing the sensing fibre in a desired location while not disturbing its free λ-T characteristic.

articleTitle: Dual active bridge converter with photovoltaic arrays for DC microgrids: design and analysis
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents an interface system based on the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter for Photovoltaic (PV) arrays for DC microgrid applications. An enhanced DC microgrid design is proposed using the DAB converter as a conversion unit in order to harvest the maximum power from the PV array. Each connected DAB converter is controlled with an enhanced control strategy. The controller is based on artificial intelligence (AI) technique to regulate the terminal PV voltage through the phase shift angle of each DAB converter. In this manner, no need for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) unit to set the reference of the PV terminal voltage. This strategy overcomes the stability issues of the DC microgrid as the response of converters is superior compared to the conventional strategies. The proposed PV interface system is modelled and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK. The simulation results reveal accurate and fast response of the proposed design in case of irradiance changes.

articleTitle: Thermal margin exploitation for increased energy yield in wind turbine permanent magnet synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper examines an intelligent operational method to extract more power out of 1.1 kW wind turbine (WT) permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) by exploiting untapped thermal potential margins. To implement this, unified multi-physical electromagnetic and thermal models of wind turbine generator are required. These were developed in different commercial software. The integrated model also consists of a new integration of pitch and field-weakening controllers that allows controlled overload operations in the constant power region by increasing generator speed and maintaining the generator terminal voltage at rated condition while increasing current magnitude, without interfering with operation in the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) region. The proposed model is tested with both fixed wind speed and a field measured wind speed profile. The simulation results show extra WT generator energy harvesting while the generator is not thermally overloaded.

articleTitle: Enhanced D-axis current demand estimation for DC-link current ripple reduction in grid-connected permanent magnet motor drives
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Conventional grid-connected AC motor drives commonly require bulky electrolytic capacitors due to the large energy ripple in the DC-link. If the energy ripple is reduced, the lifetime of the DC-link capacitor can be extended or the size of it can be significantly reduced. This paper extends upon the idea of energy control strategy in a variable speed drive with a diode rectifier input stage, supplying a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). The proposed enhanced d-axis current demand calculation includes stator resistance to provide more accurate amplitude and phase demand. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated in simulation, which shows its superior performance in reducing the 6th harmonic of the DC-link current ripple. The 6th harmonic current ripple in the DC-link capacitor has been further reduced from 4.0 A to less than 0.1 A when the stator resistance is considered in the d-axis current demand estimation.

articleTitle: Design of press-pack thyristor modules based on phase-change material cooling for SSSC short-circuit protection
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The decarbonization of power generation and consumption has led to significant transformations in future power grid operation. Power electronics equipment such as static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) offer a promising solution to integrate renewable energy sources and improve the power grid stability. However, the lack of suitable protection schemes and devices for SSSCs hinders their widespread adoption, mainly due to challenges in managing short-circuit currents. This paper proposes two design modifications to a press-pack thyristor package, which will be used for protection. First, the molybdenum and copper thicknesses are changed to enable better heat flow path. Then, phase-change material (PCM) is introduced to the design as a passive cooling solution to enhance the transient current capability of thyristors used for protection. The incorporation of PCM into customized designs enables latent heat cooling, thus, improving the thermal performance of the thyristors during shortcircuits. The efficacy of the proposed method is evaluated numerically using Finite Element Methods (FEM). The findings highlight the potential of double-side PCM-integrated designs for improving the transient short-circuit current capability.

articleTitle: Road map of power electronics knowledge and skills for enhancing engineering graduates' employability
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Undoubtedly, the power electronics industry covers a breadth of application areas and markets that many other industries can match. It is essential for the efficient conversion and conditioning of energy in a wide range of applications, for example, but not limited to smart grids and electric vehicles. Accordingly, the power electronics industry strives for more knowledgeable and skilled graduates. Hence, The electrical engineering curriculum should be supported by market-oriented knowledge and industry skills based on the industry employers' vision and recruiting plans. This paper explores the needed power electronics knowledge and skills from the perspective of industry employers. The study is based on a survey targeting 38 academics and 18 industry representatives regarding the gaps in the Power Electronics and Machine Drives (PEMD) curriculum. The survey leads to the presented road map of power electronics knowledge and skills. This road map addresses the curriculum framework and the required employability skills in the power electronics industry.

articleTitle: A novel L-shaped modular outer-rotor consequent-pole machine with unequal poles
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents a novel unequal pole L-shaped modular consequent-pole permanent magnet (UPLM-CPM) machine to improve the PM utilization ratio and torque ripple of consequent-pole permanent magnet (CPM) machines. First, a topology is presented for the proposed machines, and the simplified magnetic circuit model is applied to demonstrate the positive effect of an L-shaped modular structure with unipolar PMs on flux leakage. Then, genetic algorithm (GA) is combined with Finite element method (FEM) to optimize the width of the iron pole and flux barrier between poles with the aim of maximum average torque and minimum torque ripple. While the PM dimensions are unchanged during optimization. Finally, a comparative and finite element analysis (FEA) study is conducted for four types of machines to reveal the superiority of UPLM-CPM in terms of torque ripples, average torque, cogging torque, flux distribution, and material volume. According to the results, the proposed UPLM-CPM machine consumes 52% less PM volume, while the average torque is reduced by 2.5% compared to the modular surface-mounted PM (M-SMPM) machine, leading to the maximum PM utilization ratio. Moreover, an unequal width of PM and iron poles significantly reduces torque ripple compared to a proposed machine with equal pole width.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant grid synchronization of three-phase PWM rectifiers using neural network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This work focuses on the essential role of synchronous angle estimation in the conversion of three-phase AC to DC voltage. Accurately determining the synchronous angle is crucial for achieving optimal phasing in the abc/d–q transformation, aligning the synchronous reference d–q with the phase “a” voltage vector. This alignment ensures the efficient operation of the inner current loops in the d–q synchronous reference. However, estimating the synchronous angle becomes challenging during AC grid faults. Previous studies have employed phase-locked loops (PLLs) with specialized filters to handle parasitic harmonics. In contrast, this research proposes using neural networks to recognize fault types and estimate the phase with minimal perturbations. Comparative analyses of conventional PLL-based and neural network-based estimates of the converter bridge's output performance under fault conditions are presented using MATLAB/Simulink/PLECS.

articleTitle: Parasitic inductance and current spreading of paralleled SiC MOSFETs analysed by impedance modelling
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Paralleling silicon carbide metal-oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors in multichip power switches is a common way to achieve the required current rating in high power converters. The parasitic inductances, the static and dynamic current imbalance of the paralleled MOSFETs are limiting the maximum current and switching speed of the devices. This research investigates the effect, that the number of paralleled chips has on the parasitic inductance and the current balancing using analytical impedance analysis of lumped elements in the frequency domain. The proposed calculation approach is applied to identify the main design relevant parameters affecting the parasitic inductance and the layout-related current spreading. The results are verified with numerical parameter extractions and finite element analyses.

articleTitle: Accuracy evaluation of miner's rule to predict electrolytic capacitor damage: insights from accelerated lifetime tests
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This research study investigates the effectiveness of Miner's rule in predicting the lifetime of aluminium electrolytic capacitors. To conduct the study, a power cycling test bench is built to perform accelerated lifetime tests, subjecting the capacitors to mixed low- and high-stress conditions. The results indicate the presence of a load sequence and interaction effect, contradicting the assumptions of Miner's rule. Moreover, the results indicate that Miner's rule underestimates the amount of damage to the capacitors. Consequently, the experimental setup does not confirm the validity of Miner's rule for the lifetime prediction of aluminium electrolytic capacitors.

articleTitle: Comparison of optimisation methods for power take off design in a wave energy converter
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper describes the operation of an attenuator wave energy converter and uses it to evaluate three different simulation-based optimisation methods. The three methods are used to optimise the same flux reversal machine. Because the three methods optimise for different objective functions, they are compared using the annual energy yield each final design would produce based on a wave data set.

articleTitle: Loss analysis of a soft magnetic composite transverse flux machine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Transverse flux machines have the potential to offer high torque density in some applications. Their 3D flux path can be accommodated by making the stator from soft magnetic composites (SMC). It is generally accepted that SMC can offer low loss at high electrical frequency, but loss characteristics vary widely depending on particle size, pressing temperature, pressing pressure and component shape. This paper reports on experimental results of a 15000 rpm transverse flux machine with a segmented SMC stator. The results are used to investigate the performance of SMC within a real machine. Both no-load and load tests have been conducted, and SMC losses have been investigated using different computational models. The transverse flux machine prototype has been proved capable of delivering near 1.6 kW at 5000 rpm.

articleTitle: Enhancing short-term overload capability of wind turbine power modules with optimised heat dissipation path design and phase change material
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Phase change material was proven to absorb the extra heat and enhance the short-term overcurrent capability of the power module. However, its low thermal conductivity will impede the heat dissipation from the chips to the case. Therefore, to effectively utilise the latent heat of the PCM and mitigate the negative effects of low thermal conductivity, an optimised phase change material integration design was developed for the wind turbine power module to enhance the short-term overload capability. The PCM is integrated into the spacer between the chips of the double-side power module, which is not the main heat dissipation path. This optimised design will reduce the maximum junction temperature from 137° to 120°, and 159° to 127° under 1.2pu and 1.5pu overload conditions respectively. The integration of the PCM outside the main heat dissipation validates its effectiveness in utilising the latent heat of the PCM while mitigating the negative impact of its low thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: High power density electrical machines using air-cored high temperature superconducting coils
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The drive towards net-zero requires electrical machines with a step change in power density in future transport and energy applications. High performance materials, direct cooling methods, and superconducting coils are used to increase the power density of conventional machine technology, but with only incremental gains. The continued use of iron as the main means of focussing flux constrains the magnetic loading, so that designers cannot fully exploit the benefits of superconductors. A fully air-cored superconducting machine is introduced in which arrays of superconducting coils are arranged to produce an electromagnetic Halbach array. The elimination of iron no longer limits the magnetic field, enabling a step change increase in power density. A case study for a 1 MW direct drive generator for wind energy is used to illustrate the use of arrays of superconducting coils, and initial results indicate a 4-fold increase in power density. Cooling requirements of the superconducting coil arrays are estimated, and the mass of cryostats and cooling equipment are included in the power density calculation.

articleTitle: An improved modelling and dynamic control of the dual active bridge converter for fast battery charging of electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper investigates the control and dynamic operation of the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter applied to high-power charging of electric vehicle batteries. Starting with the presentation of the basic operation of the converter, followed by the two time-constant Thevenin-based battery modelling, an improved Fourier series-based generalized average model (GAM) of the converter is provided which considers the parasitic resistance of the output filter capacitor and is shown to have a massive effect on the dynamic operation of the converter. Furthermore, a novel combined feedforward plus feedback control system based on single phase-shift modulation is proposed for battery charging using the constant-current (CC)/constant-voltage (CV) cascaded loop strategy. The numerical results obtained from MATLAB/Simulink demonstrate the potency of the proposed control strategy and when compared to the traditional feedback-only control approach, the proposed approach shows a fast and seamless transition from the CC charging mode to the CV charging mode with very little undershoots, hence drastically improving the dynamic performance of the system with minimal controller effort, even in the presence of input voltage disturbances.

articleTitle: Simulation and testing of a newly designed half bridge module with silicon carbide MOSFET
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Carbon footprint on earth plant, lamented scenario in ‘Dans la brume’, or the unanimously adoption of Paris Agreement, all leading to the revolution and unstoppable development of electrical vehicle. Silicon Carbide (SiC), the third generation of semiconductor materials (after Thyristor and IGBT), has its greatest growth opportunity in electrical vehicles. However, opportunities always bind with problems, as for SiC, advanced packaging technologies is one of the important aspects which needs to be taken into consideration. In this paper, researchers present an improved single sided half-bridge module with cylinder connector design for electric vehicles motor drive. The design offers great power density and minimised stray parameters. Ansys Q3D and LTspice simulation are used to demonstrate the design. Different experiments on the fabricated power module are also carried out to verify the design.

articleTitle: Hybrid nanocrystalline ribbon core for 22kW automotive wireless charging
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper explores the innovative applications of nanocrystalline materials in the field of automotive wireless charging. Nanocrystalline materials exhibit several magnetic properties that are particularly advantageous for wireless charging, including high permeability and saturation flux, low core losses, and stable thermal performance. In this study, a 22kW inductive power transfer (IPT) test platform is constructed and evaluated using two novel nanocrystalline materials: nanocrystalline Ribbon Core (NRC) and nanocrystalline flake ribbon (NFR). By combining these materials and leveraging their unique properties, the IPT system achieves a peak DC-DC efficiency of over 95%. Moreover, the thermal behaviour is assessed through a long-duration 2.5kW operation, during which NFR shielding significantly enhances thermal performance. After 100 minutes of operation, the temperature rise with hybrid NFR and NRC is reduced to 50 degrees Celsius, compared to 85 degrees Celsius with the standalone NRC.

articleTitle: An all-digital generalized space vector control technique without any trigonometric calculations for higher-order multilevel inverters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: An all-digital generalized space vector control technique for the control of higher-order multilevel inverters is presented in this paper. It uses a combination of the g-h coordinate transformation technique and a space error detector to determine the nearest vector to the reference vector. The technique is free from any trigonometric calculations and is thus easily implementable using a digital signal processor. Also, the proposed technique results in the power electronic devices operating at fundamental switching frequency. Simulation results for a 21-level cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter are presented. The results are compared with simulation results using space vector modulation to prove the validity and effectiveness of the proposed technique for the control of higher-order multilevel inverters. Although the proposed technique is illustrated using a cascaded H-bridge inverter in this study, it is perfectly general and can be applied to all types of multilevel inverters, for any number of levels.

articleTitle: First order modeling and performance evaluation of a conical permanent magnet synchronous machine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this study, a first order analytical model of a conical air-gap synchronous machine is proposed. This model is built to satisfy a continuous definition from axial flux to radial flux machines. This theoretical model based on a set of assumptions is discussed and compared to a finite element method (FEM) simulations for its validation. It finally shows that this type of hybrid machine can significantly increase the torque and the mass torque density compared to conventional designs (axial or radial permanent magnet machine).

articleTitle: Analytical loss model of a three-level WBG NPC inverter comprising reverse conduction, dead time, modulation schemes and switching energy analysis
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This research derives analytical switching and conduction loss expressions for three-level WBG Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) inverters that include third quadrant operation of unipolar semiconductors and dead time states for different PWM strategies. Special attention is drawn to the topological influence on the switching energies, as it leads to additional losses compared to datasheet values measured in a two-level (2L) setup. The results of the proposed equations are verified with a numerical simulation considering thermal feedback. While the state-of-the-art analytical approach leads to a deviation by a factor of up to 1.6, the proposed method offers quick and accurate inverter loss estimation.

articleTitle: Modular power electronics integration for improved performance in C-GEN machines: simulation and experimental validation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: C-GEN machines represent a new generation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM) that embrace a remarkably modular design. These machines can be conveniently disassembled into individual parts for convenient manufacturing and maintenance purposes, thus reducing cost and enabling efficient servicing and reducing downtime. Efforts towards developing modular power electronics conversion and control aim to leverage the modularity of the C-GEN machine to improve efficiency and reliability. Within this paper, the main objective will be to investigate the benefits introduced by integrating modular power electronics and the 'electric gear' in the C-GEN machine, in terms of improving the modulation index and mitigating current distortion. To achieve these objectives, a 16kW C-GEN machine and a proposed modular power electronics topology are firstly modelled in detail using Matlab/Simulink software. A series of simulations is produced to evaluate the functionality of the modular power electronics technology and the 'electric gear'. Finally, a hardware experiment is conducted to validate the simulation results. The simulation results indicate that this modular power electronics topology can maintain a modulation index consistently above 50% and keep the current distortion lower than 5% on a wide range of rotational speed for the C-GEN.

articleTitle: The difference between published loss and measured loss in SiFe laminations and soft magnetic composite materials
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Accurate magnetic material loss prediction is preeminent to reliable and repeatable motor design using finite analysis. Two sample sizes and four materials were tested to ascertain the material loss for use in a hybrid motor design. Toroidal ring samples were made from NO20 and M250 electrical steel laminations and Soft Magnetic Composite (SMC) 700HR 5P and an experimental SMC material under development at Höganäs AB. This paper presents the discrepancy between the published loss data and measured test data.

articleTitle: Investigation of the gear ratio number impact on the cogging-torque of concentric magnetic gears with surface-inset permanent-magnets using an analytical model
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact that gear ratio has on the cogging-torque signal of concentric magnetic gears with surface-inset permanent-magnets. Initially, a generalized 2-dimensional analytical solution for the magnetic field distribution is derived, and later on the electromagnetic and cogging-torque distributions are calculated using the magnetic flux density components under different conditions. The magnetization distribution pattern used for this analysis is parallel. The analytical model is used to generate quick results with the purpose to investigate the effect of the gear ratio number on the cogging-torque amplitude of each rotor. The results showed that magnetic gears with surface-inset magnets have low torque ripple for certain gear ratios.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of dual stator hybrid excited rotary flux switching wave energy generator
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: A Dual Stator Hybrid Excited Rotary Flux Switching (DSHERFS) Wave Energy Generator (WEG) is presented with DC excitation and Armature Winding located on the outer stator and Permanent Magnets (PMs) are present in the inner stator. The generator is specifically designed for wave energy device with an average power rating of 10kW at a generator rotational speed of 30rpm. The performance of the generator is analysed, observing the coil flux linkage load voltage, average torque and output power, using FEA analysis. Hybrid nature of the machine provides flexible control of the flux density using. A design is presented giving an average torque of -4174Nm and power rating of 11kW makes it a good candidate for wave energy generator.

articleTitle: Isolated medium-voltage DC-DC power converter topologies
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents isolated DC/DC converter topologies for medium voltage applications. The main configuration of the proposed converter consists of multiple High-Frequency Transformers (HFTs) and H-bridges modules connected in series at the input (high voltage) and a multiphase rectifier at the output or parallel connected rectifiers modules. The main advantages of the proposed converters are a reduction in the DC link capacitor, elimination of the effect of mismatching multiphase transformer parameters and an increase in the output voltage gain (for boost operation). The proposed converter topologies can work as buck or boost converters. Buck converters are only considered in this paper. Different proposed connection topologies are compared with the conventional converters and Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) in terms of volume and system efficiency. Design steps for the converter, simulation results, thermal analysis and control technique are presented.

articleTitle: Control of voltage source converters under varying grid impedance in active filter applications
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents a control method of active filter under varying grid impedance conditions. The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in existing power system, changes the configuration of the power system resulting in variations of the grid impedance. For power electronics, these variations may change their behaviour and alter their control stability. An active filter is one example used for mitigating the harmonics generated by non-linear loads. They can be either of series type, where harmonic voltages are injected on the line to avoid the harmonic currents, or shunt type, where harmonic currents are injected in phase opposition with the detected harmonics. Both types mitigate the locally generated harmonics that would otherwise enter the network thus causing voltage distortion. This paper focuses on the shunt active filters which are typically voltage source converters, where a variation of the phase angle of the grid impedance will alter the injected currents that may not be in phase opposition anymore. This results in increasing the harmonic currents and deteriorates the voltage quality.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient Taguchi-based optimization of an outer rotor permanent magnet machine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: There is a growing interest in optimising the performance of permanent magnet (PM) electrical machines across numerous sectors. Their high efficiency and torque per weight ratio are very important in many applications, most notably in electrical vehicles (EV). To achieve the best performance either at a single point or across a drive cycle, it is commonplace to use numerical optimisation routines to drive finite element analysis. However, the FEM is a very time-consuming technique, and this is much worse when an optimization process requires the use of multiple operation points or three-dimensional analysis. Optimization processes such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization require many points in the design space to be simulated to find the global optima. This paper uses numerical approaches to investigate shortening the required time for the optimization process by reducing the number of finite element analysis simulations that must be run. The Taguchi method is applied to make a surrogate model from the entire design space of a case study outer rotor PM motor designed for a hybrid vehicle. Using the surrogate model, the goal function is optimized to predict the required performance. Overall, the total number of simulations for the sensitivity analysis and optimization is 52, whereas if Taguchi was not employed, 74,674 simulations are required. As each simulation takes around 162 seconds, a significant time saving is possible. Finally, all the results have been validated using ANSYS maxwell software.

articleTitle: Sensorless control technique of PMSM based on MRAS observer with smooth transition
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: A sensorless speed control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM) is proposed in this paper. Based on the Electromotive Force (EMF), the Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) observer estimates the rotor speed and position. The use of the MRAS observer instead of the stator voltage model improves the dynamics, robustness and stability of the drive system. For validation, a field-oriented speed control is implemented on a microcontroller for a PMSM. A rim thruster impeller motor is used as PMSM. Due to the small values of the stator resistance and the stator inductances, the sensorless control of the rim thruster impeller motor is associated with some difficulties. External influences, such as connection cables or temperature, can change these very small parameters considerably. In the following, a test bench is set up to implement and test the control algorithms with the MRAS observer on a microcontroller. The stator voltage model is used as a reference model for estimating the rotor speed and position. The presented method provides an effective strategy for sensorless speed control of a PMSM. A specially designed angular sliding mode ensures a smooth transition to the field-oriented control (FOC) and prevents instabilities during switching from the controlled angle to the observer's estimated angle.

articleTitle: A novel active noise cancellation method for electric motors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: With increased levels of electrification in a number of industries such as the aerospace and land transport sectors, there is growing motivation to design electric motors that have optimal performance in terms of efficiency, power density and acoustics. Motor acoustics is a key system characteristic that can have a significant impact on the target application. Acoustic noise can influence for instance the comfort of passengers onboard a commercial aircraft, the lifestyle of residents near airports or even the safety of personnel onboard a military plane or submarine. Aiming to improve the acoustics of motor drives, this paper presents a novel method of acoustic noise suppression that was named Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) by means of High Frequency Injection (HFI). The proposed method involves superimposing a high frequency voltage component to an otherwise conventional motor drive in order to create acoustic noise that is in anti-phase relation to an existing noise source and thus achieve acoustic noise cancellation. The paper presents analysis and experimental results of the proposed method being applied to the Helicopter Electro-Mechanical Actuation System (HEMAS). Although the experiments presented in this paper focus on the HEMAS platform, the method can be applied to any type of motor drive.

articleTitle: Development of a flywheel energy storage system model in RSCAD-RTDS and comparison with PSCAD
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper a detailed model of a flywheel energy storage system (FESS) for simulation in the RSCAD-RTDS platform is developed and compared with an implementation developed using the PSCAD-EMTDC program. Grid- and machine-side con-verter operation is fully considered in the developed model. The operation of the FESS under speed and DC link voltage regu-lation modes is tested in both platforms. Indirect field-oriented control (FOC) and sinusoidal PWM (SPWM) are considered for the machine control. To enable a direct, fair comparison between the two modelling platforms the PSCAD implementation follows closely the block structure and parameters used in the RSCAD version. The differences between building blocks within each simulation environment are highlighted, and simulation results are compared under charge and discharge operation modes. Contrary to previously published results, good agreement between implementations is obtained when similar parameters and equivalent blocks are used in both environments.

articleTitle: On the thermal life of poly-ether-ketone and nanofiller enamel wire insulating materials used in electrical machines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents the life of two wire insulating materials i.e., Poly-ether-ketone (PEEK) and Nanofilled enamel (Allotherm) wires, targeting the application of low voltage electrical machines where normal service operating voltage is well below the partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) throughout their lifetime. The insulation degradation has been investigated by measuring the differential dissipation factor, differential insulation capacitance and PDIV. It has been examined that the Nanofilled enamel wire loses its dielectric properties faster than PEEK. After 160h at 310°C, comparing Allotherm wire with PEEK, differential dissipation factor and insulation capacitance have been increased by 41% and 57% respectively. On the other hand, with respect to unaged condition, PDIV reduction in Allotherm and PEEK wires is 42% and 32% respectively. In terms of its mean life, PEEK wire lasted longer than Allotherm wire, giving the life percentage difference of 62.5%, 64.7% and 42% at thermal exposures 270°C, 290°C and 310°C respectively.

articleTitle: Utilising electroluminescence spectra of 4H-SIC MOSFET for bipolar degradation monitoring
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Shockley stacking faults (SSFs) due to basal plane dislocation gliding remains a concern in SiC power MOSFET. It results in SiC MOSFETs severe bipolar degradation. Electroluminescence (EL) spectra is proposed as a signature to in-situ monitor bipolar degradation. A commercial 4H-SiC MOSFET bare die was laboratory packaged and continuously stressed 2 hours upon forward current of 25A and gate voltage of -4V to accelerate bipolar degradation. Static electric characteristics and EL were measured before and after stresses. The experimental results demonstrate that an increase in bipolar degradation results in an increase in intensity and width (FWHM) of EL peaks. It indicates that EL spectra can be a powerful for online bipolar degradation monitoring in practical power conversion system.

articleTitle: Model predictive control with reduced computational burden of modular multilevel converter
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Advances in voltage source converter-based high-power applications are driven by the Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) and its variants, while the practical implementation of Model Predictive Control (MPC) faces challenges in MMCs with numerous submodules per arm. This paper proposes a Folding MPC strategy combined with a pre-processing sorting algorithm method to solve this problem. Five control objectives, including AC current, DC current, circulating current, arm energy, and leg energy, are optimized directly in a single cost function. The results show that the MMC operates satisfactorily under various operating conditions when using the proposed technique. The practical application of the MMC, even with a large number of submodules (SMs) per arm, is made possible by significantly reduction in the switching states and computational burden.

articleTitle: Grid connected power conditioning system (PCS) with energy storage
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper presents a new low cost and high efficient grid connected power conditioning system (PCS) with energy storage. Its low cost and high efficiency are achieved through the modified maximum power point tracker (MPPT) and bi-directional converter (BDC) used for energy storage integrated bi-directional inverter (BDI). The proposed PCS can achieve better performance in terms of MPPT and battery charging/discharging than the conventional PCS. A suitable current controller is employed to provide power with a nearly unity power factor and low total harmonic distortion (THD) to the utility power grid. In addition, the grid voltage is measured using a fast detection method. Thus, the proposed PCS is realized with low cost, simple structure, more effectiveness and small size. The experimental results obtained on a 1.5kW prototype show and validate the high performance of the proposed PCS.

articleTitle: Configurable, isolated voltage logging apparatus for any cell, module or fuel cell
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Voltage monitoring is essential for most electrochemical cells and modules. Many designs rely on methods that create imbalance such as potential divider ladders, or specialised integrated circuits for lithium cells that rely on connection to every cell. However, these systems do not always work with lower voltage cells such as lithium titanate, or lead acid, they also do not work if only certain cells or modules in a string are desired to be monitored, nor when multiple cells are internally connected in the form of a module. Candidates for battery energy storage including lithium titanate and lithium iron phosphate modules are available with nominal voltages of 12V and 24V, and lead acid modules are available in 6V, 8V, 12V and 24V configurations. This paper describes a flexible, configurable, high accuracy and precision voltage monitor with eight channels per board, that can be used for research grade balance monitoring experiments or general purpose use, expandable to add balancing capability. The boards can be daisy chained to monitor and log 1032 channels with up to 1000V between any of the channels. Using this circuit, any battery or fuel cell module, can be monitored with high precision without causing imbalance.

articleTitle: Design and testing of a switched reluctance motor with additively manufactured ferromagnetic cores
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This work presents an additively manufactured 8/6 switched reluctance motor prototype. The motor is designed utilising topology optimisation. The designed motor is then analysed using 2D finite element method (FEM). A prototype motor is built using laser powder-bed fusion manufactured stator and rotor ferromagnetic Fe-Co-V cores. The prototype motor is tested at several operation points, and the torque and rotation speed are measured as well as the phase voltages and currents. The measured quantities are then used to derive the mechanical and electrical power of the motor, with winding resistive and core losses. The results show that because the motor cores are solid, they suffer from high eddy current losses. However, the motor is able to produce the mechanical power that was estimated by the 2D FEM model.

articleTitle: Influence of magnetic saturation on the noise and vibration of electrical machines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: This paper investigates the origin of electromagnetic vibration and noise in electrical machines with emphasis on the magnetic saturation. An analytical model considering the slotting effect is introduced to identify the air-gap radial force harmonic and causes of them. A benchmark electrical machine and finite element (FE) analysis is used to calculate the radial force harmonic to validate the analytical model. It is found that the analytical model can predict most of the radial force harmonics but the influence of magnetic saturation cannot be included. The analysis on the benchmark motor shows that saturation can introduce higher order frequency harmonics of the lowest radial force harmonic and bring the resonance to a lower speed point. In this way, the electrical machine can suffer from noise and vibration at an earlier speed point than expected. To prove the effect of saturation, a permeance model considering saturation is introduced to validate the additional radial force harmonic contents generated by saturation. The permeance function is then extended to other slot/pole combinations and it shows that magnetic saturation has same effect on other slot/pole combinations as well.

articleTitle: Multilayer perceptron-based inductor iron loss predictions with loss map by a measurement kit
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Accurately predicting high-frequency magnetic iron losses poses a significant challenge while optimizing the design of high-frequency (HF) magnetic components and devices, such as inductors, transformers, and filters. Existing models fail to account for the complex interplay between different magnetic materials, geometry, and temperature factors, all of which have discrete and substantial effects on magnetic iron loss. In this paper, we propose a multilayer perceptron (MLP) model with techniques against overfitting for predicting iron losses based on measured data. The proposed model considers crucial parameters such as frequency, flux density, magnetic material size, as well as various materials and temperature factors. By incorporating these factors, the MLP model offers enhanced accuracy in iron loss predictions. Additionally, we introduce an automatic data measurement box specifically designed for the efficient collection of massive measurement data. These datasets serve as the training data for the proposed MLP model. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed model effectively predicts iron losses while considering all the aforementioned factors, thereby supporting its application in the design of HF magnetic devices in the future.

articleTitle: Model-based interturn short-circuit fault detection and isolation in 3-phase PMSMs with flux-linkage estimation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a detection and isolation algorithm for stator winding interturn short-circuit faults in 3-phase PMSMs is presented. In this methodology, flux-linkages are estimated in two different ways in the αβ reference frame. Based on these estimations, flux-linkage residuals are computed and used to define novel fault indicators able to detect and isolate the fault, i.e. determine the faulty phase. The novel fault indicators are defined such that they are robust against parameter mismatch. A statistical approach is then used with the cumulative sum algorithm to detect and isolate the fault. This methodology is successfully validated in simulation with a constant-parameter model in the dq reference frame able to model the machine with an interturn short-circuit fault. It is also shown that robustness against measurement noise can be achieved even with parameter mismatch. In addition, it is shown that fault detection and isolation during transients is possible when the parameters are sufficiently well estimated. Finally, this methodology is compared to a conventional signal-based approach, showing that higher sensitivity can be obtained at low fault severity.

articleTitle: Online adaptive space vector modulation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new modulation method for multilevel three-phase inverters, called online adaptive space vector modulation (oaSVM). The task of a modulator is to reconstruct the desired voltage υ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> from the available discrete voltage vectors that correspond to the inverter switch positions. State-of-the-art SVM chooses three voltage vectors that form the closest triangle containing υ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>. On the other hand, oaSVM explores every possible triangle that contains υ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> and selects the three voltage vectors such that the trade-off between inverter switching losses and load current total harmonic distortion (THD) is improved. Inverter switching constraints and neutral-point voltage balancing are also included. The resulting mixed-integer optimization problem is solved using a branch and bound method. Through MATLAB-simulations, the loss-THD trade-off between SVM and oaSVM will be compared and we show that oaSVM can improve the inverter's efficiency.

articleTitle: Robust design of six-phase segmented switch reluctance motor for a traction motor
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Recently a new trend was revealed in the development of the less rare-earth Permanent Magnet (PM) and free-PM electric machines for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications due to environmental effects, sustainability, and uncertain supply chain of the rare earth PM materials. One of the potential candidates to replace the PM-based electric machines for EV applications is the Segmented Switch Reluctance Motor (SSRM). Compared to conventional SRM, the SSRM has a higher torque density due to more magnetic utilization of the rotor core. However, this structure suffers from high torque ripple. Therefore, to overcome this issue a six-phase SSRM is presented here. First, a conceptual design based on driving cycles is carried out to specify the requirements of SSRM. Then, an initial sustainable aluminium-based design with 24 stator slots and 22 rotor segments combination is selected for further analysis. A multi-level multi-objective robust design is carried out to enhance the performance of the motor and minimize the effect of manufacturing tolerances. The optimization results indicate that the proposed method can effectively reduce the number of failed products in mass production.

articleTitle: Design concept of a repairable YASA axial flux machine with a hybrid cooling system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) axial flux machines (AFMs) offer the potential for higher torque density at a lower axial length than radial flux machines. One challenge with this particular type of machine lies in the manufacturing of the stator. Therefore, a design concept for YASA machines is developed and investigated. The design concept considers a hybrid (re)manufacturing process, which combines additive and subtractive processing steps in one production system and therefore enables a highly integrated and functionalized stator in a polymer housing. Despite the high degree of integration, the developed design concept allows the remanufacturing of individual subcomponents in the machine's stator. In addition to reparability, a special focus lies on the cooling concept of the machine in order to not exceed the low permissible temperatures of the polymer housing. In an iterative process the overall machine design is developed and a sequence of numerical simulations in three domains (electromagnetic, thermal and mechanical) is executed to investigate the operational behaviour of the machine. The final design concept fulfils the demanded requirements and therefore is a simulative proven concept. The validation of the concept via measurements is pending.

articleTitle: A magnetic analysis of ferrofluid-gaps for direct-drive wind turbine generators - an unconventional approach for reducing air-gap reluctance
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Multi-megawatt permanent magnet (PM) direct-drive (DD) wind turbine generators (WTGs) require a substantial amount of expensive rare-earth PM material in their construction due to their large air-gap radius and magnetic flux density. Conventionally, designers attempt to make the air-gap clearance as small as practicably possible to minimise the air-gap reluctance and therefore the quantity of PM material required. In this paper we investigate an alternative approach where the air-gap region is flooded with magnetically permeable ferrofluid, making it a 'ferrofluid-gap'. A brief overview of ferrofluid is given with a focus towards its suitability for use in this application. A preliminary analysis of ferrofluid-gap drag highlights that the large-size and low-speed of DD WTGs may result in acceptable efficiency losses (unlike geared WTGs). A magnetic analysis is provided of a ferrofluid-gap applied to a 3 MW DD WTG topology; shortcomings from previously published magnetic analyses of the concept are identified and remedied. Despite the relatively low saturation magnetisation of ferrofluid the results suggest that a significant amount of PM material could be saved: potentially more than 10%, which translates to over a tonne per wind turbine for power ratings greater than ~10 MW.

articleTitle: Improving energy efficiency in regional railways with PMSM
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Technological advances are committed to increasing energy efficiency, in favor of global resources preservation. Less polluting ways of using energy grow in use, with challenges associated with optimizing existing technologies. This research does, in the field of urban transport, a study for the use of the permanent magnet synchronous motor as a drive for electric traction in regional type railways, mainly in relation to the consolidated induction motor. After the theoretical review of the engineering characteristics of the electric drive, the conceptualization of properties of movement dynamics allowed obtaining data through simulations, in terms of achieved energy savings and efficiency.

articleTitle: Accurate prediction of three-phase short-circuit currents of PM synchronous machines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Since the advent of rare-earth permanent magnet (PM) materials, the PM synchronous machine (PMSM) has gained popularity in various applications, including power generation systems, industrial drives, and e-Mobility. However, the rare-earth PMs commonly used in PMSMs are inherently prone to both temperature and operation related irreversible demagnetisation risks. To realise a fault-tolerant machine design, it is essential to consider these fault conditions during the design phase of a PMSM. Traditionally, this involves time-consuming transient finite element analysis (FEA). To make it computationally more viable, fast analytical-based simulation approaches are very attractive alternatives. This paper assesses various methods for analysing dynamic three-phase short-circuit (3PSC) currents in PMSMs, with an aim to improve overall accuracy. Experimental measurements are conducted on a PMSM prototype and used as a benchmark for this study. It shows that the discrepancy between the measured and predicted results is less when machine saturation is considered. While spatial harmonic content and subtransient reactance may be neglected in the 3PSC fault simulation for specific machine types, it is crucial to exercise discretion when applying them in other scenarios.

articleTitle: Repurposing inactive oil and gas wells for energy storage: maximizing the potential via optimal drivetrain control
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing emphasis on utilizing energy storage to enhance grid resilience against disruptive events. While renewable energy supply continues to expand, gravity-based solutions like pumped hydro remain dominant in the commercial space. However, their geographical limitations constrain availability, scalability, and increase costs for co-locating solar and wind energy. An alternative approach proposes repurposing idle oil and gas wells located closer to existing grid infrastructure, offering a promising and cost-effective solution. This paper addresses the optimization and control of a regenerative drive system coupled to an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine in a 300-meter well with a 100-Newton weight. The study employs a dynamic MATLAB/Simulink model to simulate the operation of the electric drivetrain system during storage and discharge operations. The results demonstrate an initial round-trip efficiency of 85.9% for the electrical system alone and identify crucial factors for maximizing efficiency. The optimized operation and control of the electromechanical drivetrain system hold great potential for minimizing the levelized cost of storage while maximizing efficiency and revenue generation.

articleTitle: Current-to-flux linkage lookup table design for PM machinery FEA-dq hybrid dynamic models
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In recent years, a significant amount of research on modelling of electrical machines has been dedicated to high fidelity hybrid models that incorporate pre-calculated FEA data in the form of lookup tables (LUTs). Despite the increasing interest in this dynamic modelling approach, the literature largely disregards how the construction process of LUTs can impact both the accuracy of the model and the computational efficiency. This paper explores the LUT accuracy level attainable by application of various relevant data fitting interpolation algorithms and data calibration parameters using a standard permanent magnet machine geometry. It is demonstrated that an optimal trade-off between high accuracy LUT demand and the inherent high computational requirements associated with creating the requisite FEA datasets is important for facilitating effective development of hybrid model LUTs.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor control for electric vehicle powered by hybrid energy storage system: a review paper
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: The energy storage system (ESS) of an electric vehicle determines the electric vehicle's power, range, and efficiency. The electric vehicles that are available in the market currently use battery-based ESS. ESS of electric vehicles experiences a high number of charge and discharge currents which degrade the battery life span. The introduction of supercapacitors has led to the development of battery-supercapacitor hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) which takes advantage of the high energy density of batteries for drive range and the high-power density of supercapacitors to protect the battery of high charge and discharge currents. To manage the energy slit between the battery and the supercapacitor an energy management system is required. This paper reviews the different energy management strategies that have been proposed in literature.

articleTitle: Static eccentricity effect on no-load performance of FSCW PM machines with series and parallel windings
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: In this paper, static eccentricity fault is studied for open-circuit characteristics of fractional slot concentrated winding (FSCW) permanent magnet (PM) machines. Both series and parallel winding arrangements are analysed separately, and finite element and analytical methods are utilized to give full explanations about machine's performance. It is shown that Back-EMF of the surface mounted PM machine is not changed in both series and parallel winding connections after eccentricity fault. Compensation effect between phase groups and high ratio of PM to air gap thickness are responsible of such behaviour in series and parallel wound machines respectively. It is also shown that the increased cogging torque after eccentricity fault is due to interaction between the original field components (without eccentricity) and the additional components due to the eccentricity of the same order. Furthermore, it is proven than the unbalanced magnetic pull is generated due to interaction between air gap magnetization harmonics and additional eccentricity harmonics of the order differed by 1. The results presented in this paper are valid for other FSCW PM machine with various slot-pole combinations which have symmetry order of more than unity.

articleTitle: Effect of drive cycle quantification on electric motor efficiency
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: One way to evaluate real life electric vehicle performance is through drive cycle analysis . However, performing Finite Element Method (FEM) analysis is computationally heavy and optimisation of motor efficiency across all operating points using FEM is time demanding. One way to solve this is by changing the resolution of the drive cycle. The objective of this study is to investigate how different resolutions affect the results, specifically in terms of energy, losses and overall drive cycle efficiency. Thi s study shows, through both analytical calculations and FEM simulations, that it is possible to greatly decrease the number of operating points with only a minimal impact on the overall drive cycle efficiency. There does not seem to exist a universal rule to this which span different drive cycles. However, the quantifications of all drive cycles exhibit a similar pattern, with increased effic iency instability for lower resolutions. For the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure drive cycle, a decrease of 6.4 times in operating points only affects the maximum efficiency deviation by 0.036 percentage points. At this resolution, over half of the energy is distributed along only 25 points, making these a good starting point for electric motor design and optimisation.

articleTitle: A metal selection and structural optimisation methodology for large-scale direct-drive wind turbine electrical generators
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: With an ever-growing market share for offshore wind, direct-drive generators are touted as a low maintenance alternative to conventional drivetrains. However, to contend with higher torque requirements essential for low-speed operation, direct-drive machines are vastly heavier than conventional geared systems. As material use and sustainable engineering remains a key theme in the current climate, establishing methods for best practice in design stages is critical. This report therefore details a proposed methodology for the efficient, sustainable design of large-scale, direct-drive wind turbine electrical generator structures, considering mechanical, and thermal performances, whilst meeting sustainability metrics. This investigation finds that Coefficient of Thermal Expansion has a considerable influence on the maximum Equivalent Von-Mises' stress, for an optimised rotor structure under the expected loading scenario. Material choice was also found to have a significant impact on the rotor's carbon footprint and the energy use during manufacture and transport.

articleTitle: Grid forming fault ride-through capability under asymmetrical and symmetrical grid faults
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: Most current grid-connected strategies are grid-following converters (GFL), where the converter is designed to follow grid voltage and inject current into the grid. This method might not be the most satisfactory control strategy in recent years, particularly in low inertia and weak grids, due to possible interaction triggered by a phase-locked loop (PLL) during dynamics conditions. Therefore, a grid-forming converter (GFM) control mode was developed to allow the converter to emulate the characteristic of the synchronous machine as an ideal voltage source to support the grid's voltage, frequency, and grid stability during normal and fault conditions. This paper investigates the GFM converter's based Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) on Fault Ride Through (FRT) capability when symmetric and asymmetric faults are present on the grid. The proposed FRT approach for limiting the converter current uses indirect voltage control across the output of the filter inductor.

articleTitle: Advanced permanent magnet generator topologies using multimaterial shape optimization and 3D printing
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD 2023)
abstract: A vast majority of utility-scale wind turbine generators in the United States depend on foreign-sourced rare-earth permanent magnets that are vulnerable to supply chain uncertainties. Many small wind original equipment manufacturers are motivated to pursue continuous improvements to the generator design to lower the material and production costs and improve performance by lowering cogging torque and increasing efficiency. Traditional design and manufacturing offer limited opportunities. In this work, we demonstrate advanced design approaches for a 15-kW baseline wind turbine generator by making use of recent progress in three-dimensional (3D) printing of polymer-bonded magnets and electrical and structural steel. We explore three methods of magnet parametrization using Bézier curves resulting in symmetric, asymmetric and multimaterial magnet designs. We employ a multiphysics approach combining parametric computer-aided-design modeling, finite-element analysis, and targeted sampling to identify novel designs with more opportunities for reducing rare-earth material, improving efficiency and minimizing cogging torque. The results show that asymmetric-pole design and multimaterial-pole designs offer a greater opportunity to minimize rare-earth magnet materials by up to 35% with similar performance as the baseline generator, suggesting newer opportunities with design freedom beyond traditional limits of symmetry and as allowed by 3D printing.
